common_name: Sweet almond verbena / sweet almond bush
look_here_first: Find a mature opposite leaf and an intact axillary flowering raceme. Measure 5–10 fully expanded leaves (often 4–9 × 1.5–6 cm) and inspect the long, loose, often flexuose raceme: individual flower bases are visibly separated. Compare against A. gratissima's generally smaller leaves and short, crowded racemes. Do not rely on fragrance or white flower color.

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: Opposite mature leaves often substantially larger than A. gratissima

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: Flowering axes lax and flexuose, with separated flower bases

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: Usually toothed leaf margins, but variable; measure several mature leaves

lookalikes.differences: A. gratissima typically has much smaller leaves and shorter, dense flower racemes; Lantana urticoides has flowers packed into rounded heads rather than extended racemes; Verbena halei is herbaceous with spikes, not a woody shrub.
